newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia industry says wage claims dangerous.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia industry says wage claims dangerous.

text.p: The Metal Trades Industry Association of Australia (MTIA) warned on Wednesday that current union wage claims were dangerous because they were based on false assumptions about the Australian economy.
"The reality is that growth prospects in manufacturing are flat, the exchange rate is high, real interest rates are high and inflation is low," MTIA chief executive Bob Herbert said.
"Consequently, companies are finding economic conditions very difficult," he said.
Herbert said the unions should be condemned for raising employees' expectations to unrealistic levels.
"This is nothing but a short-sighted approach when unemployment is 8.6 percent," he said.
Herbert told Reuters he believed wage claims should fall in line with the inflation rate unless they were packaged with substantial productivity gains and performance improvements.
"If I were running a company, I certainly wouldn't be looking at concessions that exceed two percent unless I was making sure that they were more than offset by productivity," he said.
He said the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU), Australia's peak union body, was claiming enterprise bargaining settlements of up to 15 percent over two years.
"That's an absolute nonsense when the inflation rate is down around two (percent)," he said.
Consumer prices, excluding irregular items, rose 2.1 percent between the December quarters of 1995 and 1996.
